clusters.headline: Paraguayan Prosecutors Charge Former President Santiago Peña Following Ueno Bank Collapse
clusters.summary: Paraguayan authorities have charged former President Santiago Peña with criminal association, adding to existing charges of breach of trust and self-dealing. The charges follow his impeachment and removal from office by the Senate on November 6, 2024, amid a national financial crisis triggered by the collapse of the digital lender Ueno. Prosecutors allege that Peña used his position to direct millions in public funds to the bank, which held savings for nearly half the country's population. Peña is currently held in pretrial detention at a military facility, while Vice-President Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as his successor.
key_facts: Santiago Peña is 47 years old.
Ueno bank held approximately $800 million in public funds.
Former central bank president Carlos Carvallo was also charged.
Peña was placed under house arrest on November 6.
The bank collapse affected nearly three million people.

clusters.headline: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Trump Agree to 90-Day SNAP Rule Delay
clusters.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has secured a 90-day extension for small retailers nationwide to comply with new Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) food-stocking requirements. The agreement, reached following discussions with President Donald Trump and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, delays the original November 4 deadline. The new USDA guidelines require stores to stock at least seven varieties of items within four staple food categories: dairy, grains, protein, and fruits or vegetables. The extension takes effect on Friday and aims to prevent small businesses, such as bodegas and corner stores, from losing their ability to accept food stamps.
key_facts: The extension period is 90 days.
The original compliance deadline was November 4.
New rules require seven varieties in each of four staple food categories.
Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins participated in the discussions.
Mayor Mamdani had previously requested a six-month postponement from the USDA.

clusters.headline: Chicago Chief Financial Officer Ashlee Gabrysch Resigns After Three Months
clusters.summary: Chicago Chief Financial Officer Ashlee Gabrysch resigned on Friday after serving in the role for only three months. In her resignation statement, Gabrysch cited an inability to provide complete and accurate financial information without compromising her professional integrity. Her departure marks the third time the city has lost a CFO within a single year. The resignation has prompted calls for an investigation and raised concerns regarding the city's credit rating during a contentious budget season.

Gabrysch served in the role for three months before resigning.
The resignation occurred during a stalemate between Mayor Brandon Johnson and the City Council over the 2027 spending plan.
Gabrysch stated that CFO financial statements must be 'complete and accurate' for investors and rating agencies.

clusters.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following reports of multiple extramarital affairs
clusters.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12, 2026, following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs. Reports indicate Huang misled company leadership, including general counsel Tim Teter and CMO Alison Wagonfeld, by characterizing his relationship with Alice Huang as standard business dealings. Alice Huang is a Singapore-based executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy. Following the scandal and an independent probe by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, Nvidia shares have declined by more than 30%.

Alice Huang is an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed.

Jensen Huang is 63 years old.

clusters.headline: China warns against new US chip export controls following Nvidia scandal
clusters.summary: China has cautioned the United States against implementing further export restrictions on semiconductors following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a scandal that has drawn scrutiny toward his business ties with Beijing. Reports indicate that Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a firm linked to the scandal, allegedly obtained banned Nvidia H800 chips. Chinese officials argue that additional export controls would disrupt global supply chains and harm international interests.
key_facts: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO following an admitted affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing reportedly obtained servers containing Nvidia H800 chips.
Foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning stated China opposes the abuse of export control measures.
The scandal may impact the upcoming expected meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
The servers were reportedly purchased from Dell Technologies via Aperia Cloud Services.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While Western outlets focus on the security implications of the scandal and potential export controls, Chinese observers and state-aligned commentary frame the professional downfall of Jensen Huang as a politically motivated hit.

clusters.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russian oil hub in Samara and airfield in Lipetsk
clusters.summary: On November 13, Ukrainian forces conducted long-range drone strikes against a key oil-pumping station in Russia's Samara Oblast and the Lipetsk-2 military airfield. The Security Service of Ukraine and the General Staff confirmed the attack on the Samara linear production and dispatch station near the village of Prosvet, which resulted in a fire and damage to oil storage tanks. The Samara facility is a critical hub for blending crude oil into the Urals export blend. Ukrainian officials stated the strikes were part of ongoing efforts to target Russian infrastructure.

Samara facility is located near the village of Prosvet

clusters.headline: Mexican President Sheinbaum denies migrant caravans are traveling toward the US border
clusters.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stated on Friday that no migrant caravans are currently moving toward the United States border. She clarified that while two caravans were identified in Mexico, one has already dissolved and the other is only in the early stages of formation. This statement follows a threat from US President Donald Trump to double tariffs on Mexican goods if the country fails to stop migrant groups from reaching the border. Trump has characterized the movement of these caravans as an invasion of the United States.
